# V1 requirements — input to installed spec-driven-dev skill

**State:** `DRAFT_INPUT`, **not** the canonical spec generated by the installed skill. Convert these statements to the exact artifacts mandated by that skill. Keep requirement IDs stable so tests remain traceable. No external service use is permitted during this assignment.

## Functional requirements

### R-01 — Sheet input and stable identity
Read a selected, explicit Sheet tab (ID/gid, not `getActiveSheet()` inside the engine). Require unique `Email Address` and `Mail Merge Status` headers. Support a configurable header row only if needed; favor row 1 by default. Read displayed values when preserving user-facing strings and leading zeros. Treat case/spacing-duplicate headers as invalid. Never overwrite arbitrary existing columns.

### R-02 — Templates
Use one specific Gmail draft as a template; identify it unambiguously (stable draft ID or explicit selection validated before send, not first match by subject). Support subject, plain text, HTML, common attachments and inline images where the Google API permits. Preserve formatted content and links. Errors reading the template fail closed.

### R-03 — Variables
Replace `{{Exact header}}` in subject, text and HTML with the row's value. Do not silently erase missing or unresolved tokens. Escape values for HTML *text* context, sanitize subject/header CR/LF, never interpret column values as executable HTML. If attribute/URL insertion is proposed, apply context-aware validation or disallow in V1. Distinguish an empty optional field from an actual required field; initial conservative rule: a referenced placeholder must resolve to a non-empty value, unless documented otherwise.

### R-04 — Destination and sender
Read exactly one recipient from `Email Address` per row; no merging rows by email and no implicit BCC of other recipients. Validate format conservatively. Allow a Gmail-authorized sender/alias and optional Reply-To if supported; reject unavailable aliases before any send. CC/BCC may be omitted entirely from V1 unless confirmed necessary; if included, count recipient quota and validate identities.

### R-05 — Drive attachments
Parse zero or more Drive links from `File Attachments`, separated by commas. Preserve common attachments on the Gmail draft and append only row-specific files. Validate every provided link/ID, file permission, type, conversion and aggregate size BEFORE sending. Existing binary PDFs/files retain their original blob; Google-native Docs/Sheets/Slides convert to PDF via supported APIs. If any requested attachment cannot be resolved, **block the row**; never change Drive sharing ACL, never instruct user to set public access.

### R-06 — Exclusions and legacy statuses
Only a blank `Mail Merge Status` is eligible by default. `SKIP`, `Email Sent`, dates, errors, `SENDING`, `REVIEW` and **any nonblank unexpected value** are excluded until manually resolved. Manually hidden and filter-hidden rows are excluded. Read visibility from the **explicit target Sheet**. The preflight summary must count exclusions separately from validation failures.

### R-07 — Preflight and snapshot protection
Preflight is read-only and must report: selected tab, draft identity/subject, sender, count eligible/excluded/invalid, missing variables, attachment issues and available quota estimate. Create a digest/snapshot of the campaign's intended recipients, subject, variable values and attachment IDs; at execution detect changed input and either invalidate the confirmation or revalidate each affected row before attempting a send. Do not send unreviewed changed data.

### R-08 — Representative test
Use the same renderer and same attachments pipeline as actual send, changing only the destination to a specifically approved test mailbox and marking the subject `[TEST]`. Do not alter `Mail Merge Status` or create false records of production sends. In this assignment execute **mock tests only**; no live mail to any mailbox.

### R-09 — Explicit human send decision
A real send path must require an operator action and a second confirmation showing the exact source, sender and number of eligible rows. No sending on `onOpen`, scheduled execution, project installation or test run. Implement the button/controller locally with mocked services; do not invoke a real provider endpoint during this assignment.

### R-10 — Single execution
Use a document/script lock appropriate for a bound Apps Script project, document the choice, and ensure simultaneous calls cannot claim a row twice. No race between two tabs/users. Prefer stable campaign and row IDs over relying only on current row index if row order changes.

### R-11 — Per-row checkpoint and ambiguity
Before calling Gmail, persist `SENDING` (or equivalent claim) for that row and flush/check success. After Gmail returns without error, record `Email Sent` (or provider-compatible success) and timestamp. If execution or persistence fails around Gmail, the state must remain `SENDING`/`REVIEW`, not automatically be made pending again. A failed send call can be ambiguous; never promise exactly-once delivery. Manual review must be required to authorize a retry.

### R-12 — Batches, runtime and quotas
Inspect the current remaining recipient quota through the provided API; count all To/CC/BCC recipients if supported. Stop conservatively before six-minute Apps Script cap and at quota exhaustion. No magic sleeps or invented guaranteed throughput; process safe pending rows in a later manual run. Do not automatically schedule continuation in V1.

### R-13 — Minimal audit
Maintain status in Sheet plus a small append-only or equivalent log, recording timestamp, campaign ID, stable row reference, destination (only necessary data), phase/outcome and actionable error. Do not log entire row snapshots, full email body, Drive URLs, private file content, API tokens or other unnecessary personal data. Never mislabel `accepted by Gmail API` as `delivered to recipient`.

### R-14 — Minimal operator interface
Use a Sheet menu: `Validar`, `Vista previa / prueba`, `Enviar pendientes`, `Ver registro` (wording may change). Add a small HTML sidebar **only if needed** to select an unambiguous Gmail draft and show confirmation/preflight. No dashboard or independent web interface; UI actions must connect to tested backend functions, not placeholders.

### R-15 — Local development and exit criteria
Ship runnable Apps Script source, an explicit manifest, offline Node tests/mocks, synthetic fixture data, a setup/operations guide, a manual future deployment checklist and a clear acceptance-status report. Use local Git with incremental commits. No Git remote, Google login, new Apps Script project, `clasp` uploads, real sends or live OAuth during this assignment.

## State machine (proposed; formalize during design)

```text
blank PENDING ── preflight invalid ──> validation report (no send)
blank PENDING ── lock + claim persist ──> SENDING
SENDING ── Gmail API accepted + persist success ──> Email Sent
SENDING ── crash / ambiguous exception ──> REVIEW (manual reconciliation)
Email Sent / SKIP / REVIEW / other nonblank ──> excluded from automatic runs
```

Important: a pure validation failure need not write a permanent status or block correction. Any post-claim exception must be treated as uncertain unless the system can prove no message could have been submitted. A mock of Gmail is not evidence of real delivery.

## Nonfunctional contracts
- **Simplicity:** target one small bound Apps Script app, no runtime dependency on external libraries.
- **Testability:** pure functions separated from Google APIs; offline tests run with no credentials/network. No mocks in production path.
- **Reproducibility:** one documented local command to run all relevant tests; logs of actual results.
- **Security:** least privilege scopes, no public Drive shares, no external telemetry; reviews before any future live environment use.
- **Usability:** reuse current column names, clear errors, no hidden default send action.

## Out of scope
Scheduled Date execution, trigger-based autosend, Gmail bounce/open/click tracking, consent-management product, dynamic PDF generation, CRM/ERP sync, bulk importing of contact lists, marketing segments, independent web app, paid external service, analytics dashboard.

## Key design risks for the skill to resolve
1. Identify exact common + per-row attachment shape and how to preserve Gmail inline images without breaking HTML.
2. Store row claim before send in a way that survives partially completed executions.
3. Avoid choosing an arbitrary draft by subject.
4. Avoid stale preflight values when users edit/reorder the sheet.
5. Find the smallest viable boundary between pure logic and Apps Script services, without bundlers or a complex layer system unless justified.
6. Verify Apps Script file formats and manifest, minimal OAuth scopes and quotas from current official docs; do not assume test runners can execute Google services offline.
